questions.q: What is the telltale sign of 'Category One' ADFdi failures — the tool itself not working?
options: A detailed business-rule error message about a specific invoice
A scheduled process report showing rejected rows
Nothing related to actual data ever gets a chance to matter — the ribbon doesn't appear, or an action does nothing when clicked
An interface table filling up with stale data
questions.explain: Category One failures are environment/setup problems — the add-in, macros, or security settings — and they prevent any data-related action from even starting.

questions.q: What is the correct first step when an ADFdi 'Create ___ in Spreadsheet' action does nothing when clicked?
options: Assume the entered data is wrong and start re-typing it
Submit a request to change the chart of accounts
Purge the interface table immediately
Check the add-in installation, macro settings, and security/trust settings, before assuming anything about the data
questions.explain: When the tool itself doesn't function, the data hasn't even been given a chance to be evaluated — the fix is in the installation and security prerequisites, not the data.

questions.q: How does 'Category Two' ADFdi failures (a row being rejected) compare conceptually to FBDI rejections?
options: They stem from the same underlying business rules (balancing, existing references, matching totals) — only the delivery mechanism and timing of the error differ
They are unrelated — ADFdi has no business-rule validation at all
ADFdi rejections can never be fixed
ADFdi only rejects rows randomly with no real cause
questions.explain: The business rules themselves don't change based on the tool used. ADFdi just surfaces rejections immediately and inline, rather than in a later scheduled process report.

questions.q: What 'trap' does ADFdi's immediate feedback create, according to this lesson?
options: It makes all business-rule validation disappear entirely
It can tempt a user into resubmitting the entire spreadsheet after fixing only one row, instead of resubmitting just the corrected rows
It forces the user to wait longer than FBDI for feedback
It requires purging the interface table before every resubmission
questions.explain: The same discipline that applies to FBDI — fix only what failed and resubmit only that — still applies to ADFdi, even though its faster feedback loop can tempt a user to skip that discipline.

questions.q: When troubleshooting an ADFdi issue, what should be checked FIRST if the tool won't launch or upload at all?
options: The specific business-rule content of the data being entered
The UCM account configuration
The add-in installation, macro settings, and trust/security settings
The GL_INTERFACE table
questions.explain: If the tool itself isn't functioning, the problem is almost certainly in setup and prerequisites (add-in, macros, security), not in the specific data being entered — and UCM/GL_INTERFACE are FBDI concepts, not relevant to ADFdi at all.
